utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honours. For Zupljanin Defence, Igor Pantelic and Dragan Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just before the witness puts the earphones on, can I just mention that -- at the end of this afternoon can I mention two administrative matters which won't occupy very long, and shouldn't, I don't think, involve an argument today. Second, these: Can I just give Your Honours a very, very brief outline of Kljuc, because we're moving to a new municipality, and the witness is going to be asked to look at some photographs and identify things which relate to matters that happened. The events in Kljuc are very largely covered at the moment by adjudicated facts which, of course, apply to Stanisic but not at the moment to Zupljanin. The events include two major killings. The first on June the 1st of 1992 at the Velagici school in which inhabitants of villages had been taken and confined for a short period of time. And on the 10th of July, Biljani school, again in which inhabitants of local villages had been taken to after the Prosecution say they'd been rounded up. We are not calling any evidence in relation to either of those killings because they are covered pretty completely at the moment by adjudicated facts. In addition to that, non-Serbs who had been rounded up were confined in the police station and in the Nikola Mackic school in which we say beatings took place. Again, Your Honours. There will be no evidence about that because it's covered by adjudicated facts. The witness you're about to hear, Mr. Egrlic, has testified in both the Brdjanin and the Krajisnik cases. He was, as you will hear, the President of the Executive Board of the SDA in Kljuc. And the other Muslim party in Kljuc was the MBO, the Muslim Bosniak association -- organisation, which was headed by Omer Filipovic about whom you've also heard. The SDS was headed by Veljko Kondic or Jovo Banjac. And his relative, that is, say, Mr. Veljko Kondic -- Mr. Vinko Kondic, at the relevant period was chief of the SJB. You will not be hearing from Mr. Vinko Kondic because he's presently standing trial in Sarajevo in the state court. Mr. Egrlic's evidence covers the events leading to the takeover, including a meeting with Stojan Zupljanin about which, although it's covered in his transcript, I'm going to ask for a little detail about. The SDS took over power in Kljuc on the 7th of May, and without any resistance at all at that stage. There was an order issued for the surrender of all weapons, and violence really started on or about the 27th of May when two Serb soldiers were killed at check-points which had been set up at the village of Pudin Han. The non-Serb villages were attacked. People were killed during the attacks, and those who survived were rounded up and imprisoned. Mr. Egrlic, by the 27th of May, along with many other Muslim inhabitants, had fled to the woods. During of course of those events he apparently managed to wound himself with his own pistol and was on his way to seek medical assistance when he was arrested by the Bosnian Serb police at a check-point. He was taken to the Kljuc SJB. The evidence in his transcript is to the effect that he was beaten there, then taken to hospital, from there to Stari Gradiska prison and from there to Manjaca together with many, many of the other inhabitants of Kljuc, as Your Honours will have seen. And he remained in Manjaca until December of 1992. Your Honour, that's a brief summary of the events relating to Kljuc. So if we can now perhaps deal with Mr. Egrlic's preliminaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I understand the Stanisic team may have had a preliminary matter before the witness was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There is one matter. We're doing it now, although it could be done later. It's in regards to the 92 ter package. We anticipate the witness will adopt his previous testimony from both Brdjanin and Krajisnik. And that being done, you will admit his two transcripts and the documents on the 65 ter package. Now, there are approximately ten exhibits in total, that's our estimate, from those two trials which we would like to have admitted into the record, and we are proposing to do that by way of motion so that we can give you a cross-reference to the exhibits in the previous case so you can see the relevance, but they're linked to his testimony but they're not being offered by the Prosecution, and we would like to offer them as part of a package to go along with his testimony. And we propose to do that by way of motion very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It would be helpful if you could indicate the ten exhibits that you wish to have included before you begin your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, we may not even have any cross-examination. But these documents are -- were referred to during his testimony in the previous trials. Some questions were put by the Prosecution, some by the Defence. He will adopt those -- that testimony and give the same answers today, he will likely say, and we say fine. We just want to have those ten documents in the record so that you, when you evaluate the testimony, will have the full picture. So the Prosecution has made it's selection; we are proposing to make ours, and it's about ten. And if that being the case -- in fact there's no point in cross-examining this witness on those ten documents. We accept what he said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As may have been explained to you, you are called to give evidence as a witness in this trial which is taking place in The Hague, and we're receiving your evidence by way of videolink. Do we understand correctly that you have testified previously in two trials?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, I need then only remind you of the procedure that is followed in terms of -- as far as you being a witness goes. The side calling you, in this case the Prosecution, would have questions of you, and because of the mode in which you are being offered as a witness, their questions would be somewhat abbreviated from how it otherwise would have been. After that, the side opposite, if they wish, that is both -- counsel for both accused persons, would have the right to ask you questions. The Prosecution could then re-examine, and the Court itself may have questions of you. I would begin by asking you to state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Asim Egrlic is my name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 27 July 1952, in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I again for the second day in a row have forgotten to ask the Court Officer to administer the solemn declaration. If you would, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. You may resume your seat. Continuing with the introductory questions, what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I thought it was on. I'll ask again. What is your profession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a degree in architecture, and I'm engaged in design.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, good afternoon. I don't know whether you can see me.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's been a long time since we met, but I would still recognise you. Right. I don't think there's anything you can say to that. Can I first of all start by just establishing, please, that as you said, you testified in both cases -- two cases, that of the case against Brdjanin and Talic, and secondly, in the Krajisnik case. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review your testimony in both of those cases?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if asked those questions that you were asked on the last occasion, in particular those in the Brdjanin case, would your answers still be the same?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just going to ask you a little bit about some of the matters that you were asked about in the other trials. First, you told the Court that you were an architect, but were you also, in 1990, president of the SDA party in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was there in fact another Muslim political party in Kljuc, the MBO?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that headed by the late Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally, the SDS. Who was the head of the SDS in Kljuc in the 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm afraid you'll have to repeat your answer. The interpreter didn't pick it up.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Veljko Kondic was the head of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want, I'm afraid, to do a rather torturous thing, which it is to go through a map and some photographs which you've had an opportunity to look at when you were seen in Sarajevo. Can we start, please, with the map which is behind divider, in your bundle, number 74. 65 ter number is 10236.09. Right. Now, Mr. Egrlic, this map shows the ethnic breakdown of Kljuc effectively after the census or at the time of the census. And are these figures correct? There was a small number of Croats there, 330. 18 -- 18.500 Serbs roughly, and 17.700 Muslims in the Kljuc municipality at that time. Would you agree that's correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the map shows really the breakdown of the various villages, and it looks, and again this is very rough, but as though the Muslim areas were largely congregated to the north of Kljuc town which is shown in the middle and the Serb areas to the south and east?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is this also correct, that the town itself seems to have been largely Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, there seems to be a problem here which is going to slow things down even more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm very sorry, you're going to have to repeat your answer again.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as the town of Kljuc is concerned, the ethnic composition there was mixed, and Serbs may have had a bit of an advantage when it came to the number of inhabitants there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. In that case, that's all I want to ask you about that map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P921, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. I mislaid my note at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In a moment I'm going to ask you to look at some photographs of the town and other areas, but there's one thing I forgot to ask you. Who was the chief of police in Kljuc in -- after the elections?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't understand what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Chief of police was Vinko Kondic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just pause a minute. Your Honours, I think we ought to clear up what the problem is, otherwise this is going to take a long time. Why are the interpreters are having this difficulty?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sometimes it's simply unintelligible what the witness said. The sound breaks, and we cannot understand what he said, and other times the sound is good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If the experience from yesterday's testimony serves to any purpose, then I would suggest that the witness be instructed that he speaks directly down into the microphone on the table.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's see how we get on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, it's not your fault, don't worry. I'm afraid it's one of the problems. Next thing I want you to look, please, at is an overview of Kljuc which you will find behind divider 54. It's an aerial photograph. And the 65 ter number is 10260.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It might help to tilt it the other way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So this is an aerial view taken last year. If we go to the centre of the photograph, we can see a building with a blue roof, which we will see in close up in another photograph. Are you able to tell the Court what that is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The building in the centre with a blue roof is the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And I think we'll -- for the other buildings we'll look at the close-up. Sir, you testified last time that before you were arrested in -- on the 28th of May, you had taken to the woods. Can we see those woods anywhere in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was taken to the SUP. That's the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, but before you were, as I say -- as you were caught and taken to the SUP, you'd left the town of Kljuc, hadn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And whereabouts were you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was with my family in the forest. The family -- my family was expelled from our house just like other residents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And what I'm asking is whether it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Terribly sorry. Your Honours, I'm not getting Ms. Korner on my earphones or any of the translators, and it's -- it's very hard for me to follow because I'm following what the witness is saying, and I can't hear the question. I don't want to -- I don't want to interrupt you, Ms. Korner. You can continue, but if this can be dealt with, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought you were going to say it was a blessed relief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I meant to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm sorry for that small digression. One of the Defence counsels is having a problem hearing you. But, yes, it is the forest. Is one able to see the forest where you were with your family in this photograph? That's all I was asking.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, one cannot see it. It's in the broader area to the north-east of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then don't worry about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that photograph be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Exhibit P922.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And now can you go in on a closer view, and that's in divider 75, the last one in the bundle, and it's 10265.16. Right. Thank you. Now, I think we can see a closer view there of what you've already identified as the SUP with the blue roof in the middle of that photograph. Can you point out to us, please, next where the courthouse was in Kljuc? Now -- yes. Can you -- I think you have to mark it with a pen, and I don't know -- I can't remember what happens. Do we hold it up, or what?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The courthouse was across from the police station, here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then if we can hold it up to the camera just so that the Judges can see and everybody. Is it possible to see that? No. The colour -- oh, I see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do Your Honours see that? There's a circle. It's not terribly clear. Towards the left-hand side of the picture, as it's being shown. The colours don't seem to work like this, which doesn't help much. But if you look, there's the -- the SUP is just to the right of where the -- it's being held up, and then there's a circle round the building opposite. Do you see that? No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Then I think if you -- sir, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What we'll do is we'll mark it. It will come back. But I can indicate because I've got the advantage of seeing this before. Your Honours, could we have the photograph back on the screen that Your Honours were looking at. Is it on the screen? Your Honours, what he marked and where it is, it's opposite the blue building which is the SUP. There's a building with a roof there, which is being indicated at the moment. That's where the courthouse was. I said this was going to be slow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Nest, could you indicate, please, where the Nikola Mackic school is.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Can we have --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if nobody minds, I will actually just tell Your Honours. You can see it now, yes. It's the building. There's a sort of white what looks like a football pitch, and that's the Nikola Mackic school. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally, we can see in the middle of the photograph, there's a square building, part of which appears to have red roofs and part of which appears to be a grey roof. Can you just the Court what that is.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's the municipal building and the building of the Municipal Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was there a TO building in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. This wing to the right behind the municipal building is the building of the TO.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it's all effectively part of the same complex, the municipal building and the TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The photograph, this photograph, effectively shows two roads, one at the back of all the buildings and one that we can see in the front. In 1992, did the road at the back exist?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir -- Mr. Egrlic. You've been asked to repeat again.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There was a road behind the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: After the Serbs took power on the 7th of May, were roadblocks set up?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were -- were roadblocks set up anywhere that we can see within that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Here at the crossroads between the road which links up the police building and the main street.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, sir, can you mark it? And again, hold it up to the camera. Yes. I think we can see where that is. Yes. Just to the right of the municipal building as one looks at the photograph. Yes. Thank you very much. That's all I'll ask you about that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can that be marked -- admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, but I have a question. The -- inasmuch as the -- it's the same print that has been used for, I think, now four indications by the witness, he wasn't asked to number them, he was just asked to circle them. When it comes back to us, how are we going to remember what is what?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, you've asked -- you've been asked to mark this before, but can you mark by the -- what did I ask you first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The first thing that you identified was the court building. Could you mark that as number 1.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then the second thing you identified -- thing, building, was the Nikola Mackic -- Mackic school. Could you mark that with 2.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The -- the municipal building with the TO as 3.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then the roadblock as 4.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And thank you very much, sir. And that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May that -- oh, it has already been marked and admitted, hasn't it. No. Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P923.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can you now move to your divider 56, please, because we can see another shot but from another angle. And that's 65 ter 10262. Now, are we now looking again at the sort of centre of Kljuc town but from the other side of the -- effectively the municipal building, which again is in the centre? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think we need to go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, Your Honours, may I simply ask that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P924, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I now want you to look, please, at some other photographs, this time of the Nikola Mackic school, starting with divider 50, and that is 65 ter 2185. Now, this is a photograph that was -- that was taken a little bit nearer the time, Mr. Egrlic. In fact, as you can see from the legend, on the 21st of July, 2001. Do you recognise that as the Nikola Mackic school?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did it look -- this is 2001. Did it look much the same or was it different in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It looked the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And if you go to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. May that be admitted, please, and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P925, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you go now, please, to divider 60, which is 65 ter 10265.02.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph of the school with the school playground.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, unfortunately, is not on our screen yet, but thank you, sir. Yes. I don't think you were taken there, sir, but are you aware that people from -- who had been rounded up, non-Serbs, were kept in -- in those premises?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that they were at the school and at the gym right next to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then I think one more photograph, please, of that. Can you look --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. May that be admitted and marked, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P926, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your divider 61, Exhibit 10265.3. And what are we looking at there, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We can see the gym hall here next to the school building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be marked and admitted. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P927, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next can we have a look at a couple of photographs of the SJB building, please. For you, divider 51. And the 65 ter is 2184. Mr. Egrlic, can you identify that as -- as the SJB building, the front of it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told the -- the Trial Chambers in both the Brdjanin and the Krajisnik case that when you were taken to the SUP you were beaten. In fact, beaten outside. Can you show the Court whereabouts you were beaten.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Here at these stairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, just in case anybody wants to know, that is dealt with in the Brdjanin transcript at page 10559 and there on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mrs. Korner, is this the building that on the first photos we saw had a blue roof?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I should -- I better ask the witness, but I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, in this photograph in 2001, it had this colour roof. In the photographs that we saw taken last year, it had a blue roof. Is this one and the same building there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same building, but the roof was changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I saw Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry -- I lost my note again. Oh, Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P928, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if you go to your divider 59. And it's 10265.1, 65 ter number. Is that the -- the same building or part of the same building?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We can see the stairs there are to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could that be marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P929, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And finally, can I ask you -- within Kljuc town, can I ask you to look, please, at divider 62. And 10265.4. And perhaps you can tell us, Mr. Egrlic, what that particularly repellent coloured building is.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In this building there are a number of premises. There is the conference hall of the Municipal Council, part of the TO premises were housed here, and also there are some additional offices.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that's part of that square complex that we saw from the air; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if one looks at the left of the photograph, is -- is that the part of the school that we're looking at?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We see part of the school and the gym.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be marked and admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P930, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, now I want to take you out of Kljuc town, please, for some photographs. Could you look at divider 52, and that is 10258. Sir, can you tell us what we're looking at there in the middle of the picture -- photograph?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We see the Biljani settlement here, and then in the centre of the photograph is an a graveyard with a mosque and culture hall.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In 1992, was that mosque there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. There was a local school in this spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what does the graveyard represent? Well, that's not quite the way of putting it. The people who are buried in that graveyard next to the mosque, where are they from?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They were found in a mass grave in Biljani. They were exhumated and reburied.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is it known where they met their deaths, the people who are buried there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They were shot to death in the settlement here, mostly around the school building, in front of that building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And sorry, the road we can see going off to the right, is that the road that leads towards Kljuc town?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P931, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then can we go to just a closer view of that. It's divider 53 for you, Mr. Egrlic, and it's 10259.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, all those photographs are part of the sequence that were taken last year. And I think it's clearer there. We can see the graveyards. Yes. Thank you. Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P932, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next can you go, please, in your bundle to divider 58, 10264, please. Can you tell us, please -- tell the Court, please, Mr. Egrlic, what's shown in this overview.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Velagici. That's what is shown in the overview. You can see the crossroads of a road leading to Laniste, Bosanski Petrovac, and the left-hand side road leads towards Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So going towards the right-hand side of the photograph is the lows to Laniste; is that right? Did you hear that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't have interpretation. I did not hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let me try again. Road to -- as it goes off the right of the photograph, does that road go to Laniste?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The road to Laniste is to the right from the central part of the photo, from the crossroads.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And Velagici, we -- and -- sorry, before -- my fault. Forget that. Were units of the -- what was to become the Bosnian Serb army, the VRS, stationed in Laniste during the May period?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't -- I don't think you can help. Can you tell us which unit in particular?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that some elements of units arrived from Knin, from the Knin Corps, and we were replenished with local Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about the 60th Partisan Brigade? Did you ever come across them at all? Led by Colonel Basara.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The 6th Krajina Brigade occupied Kljuc -- occupied Kljuc on the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The 6th Krajina Brigade. That's my fault. It was part of the 60th Partisan. Can you tell us, sir, in the middle of the photograph where the crossroads is, what are we looking at there, the squared-off bit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We can see a cemetery which was created after the exhumation of Bosniaks who had been killed and buried in the Laniste 2 mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And where had those people been killed? Was it -- was that established?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They were executed by the local school which used to stand in the place of the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P933, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we then go -- we can look at a -- sorry, I've made a -- yes. To 57, I think it is. That's a closer view of it. Yes, 57. Sorry, which is 10263. And there, I think, we can see a closer view of the crossroads, and in particular, the graveyard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be marked and admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P934, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't think we need bother.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like you to have a look at a whole series of photographs, please, sir, which I'll have up on the screen one after the other. They start, please, in your binder at 66. And it's 10265.8. Now, I'm not sure how clear these are going to be, but hopefully clear enough. Yes. This is a whole series of photographs taken at the Velagici cemetery. First of all, sir, there we can see two people named on the graves. Not a great picture, I agree, but -- in fact, I contact read that one. But firstly did you know either of those two people?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them, but the family names --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the witness properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll have to say it again, sir, by leaning into the microphone. I don't know whether it's possible -- sorry. You said you knew the families of these --

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know them personally, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just -- your copy may be better than what we can see on the screen, but does the first gravestone show that it was 1912 to 1992 and the second 1899 to 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can that be admitted and marked, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I do apologise. Your Honours, maybe my learned friend Ms. Korner could ask Mr. Egrlic, in order to spare time for cross-examination in light of judicial economy, just to read what is -- what are the other terms here on -- on this yard -- stone, simply for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you're being asked to read what else is on that stone. Are you able to do that, sir? The photographs aren't great, I'm afraid, or the copies aren't great.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Arif Pajic and Junuz Pajic. That's all I can see. There are some other gravestones, but I can't see anything on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Don't worry about the names. There's something written above the names. I think that's what you're being asked about. It may be clearer on the next photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask that this one be marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we will have a look. Can you look now --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P935, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you look now behind number 67 for you, and it's 10265.9. Right. First question is can you read what the word is above the name of Mr. Junuz?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It says Sehid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which means? What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's a title given to those who were killed as innocent victims.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And again I think we can see he was born in 1899. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P936, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The one behind divider 68. 10265.10. Mr. Arif Pajic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we have that, please, admitted and marked and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you, and next --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P937, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And next behind divider 69. 10265.11. Selva Draganovic. Did you know -- is that a him or a her? Sorry, did you know him or her? Draganovic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I knew that woman, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did -- as far as you know, did she have anything to do with armed resistance to the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, nothing whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P938, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And very quickly then. The last two are at, for you, divider 70, 10265.2. Actually, it's three, last three. Three more. .12, sorry, what did I say? .12, yes. Did you -- sir, did you know him, Mr. Nezic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P939, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then number 71. 10265.13. This was a five-year-old child, it looks like, Mr. -- Mr. Becirevic. Did you know the Becirevic family or this child?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know the child, but I'm familiar with the family name. It does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P940, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next one, please, number 72. 10265.14. Mina Ticevic. Is that a man or a woman?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: A woman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know her?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't know her, but I know the Ticevic family.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P941, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is the final photograph behind number -- divider 73, and it's 10265.15. Another Draganovic, Mr. Egrlic. Did you know him, Ibrahim Draganovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who was 70-odd, 71, at the time of his death. Do you know how he came by his death?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: May that be marked and admitted, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P942, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've just got two more photographs that I want to -- three, maybe, ask you about. Can you go to divider 63, for you, please, and it's 10265.5. Yes. Can you -- tell us what we're looking at there.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I believe that this is one part of Pudin Han settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you can't answer this question, Mr. Egrlic, say so straight away: Do you know where the check-point was, where the guards had been set up before the incident that took place on the 27th of May? If you don't, say so straight away.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know in the town of Kljuc and in Velagici, I know about those check-points, and I know that there was one at the crossroads of a road leading to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you're not able to say in relation to Pudin Han where the village guards were stationed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that we understand each other. I thought that you were asking me about police check-points, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to know if you're able to identify the point -- we know that there was an incident when two Serbs were killed around Pudin Han. Are you able to identify in this photograph where that was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's not shown in the photo, but it would have been to the right from the part depicted in the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be -- may that be marked and admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P943, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, finally, the photographs that we saw, the modern ones, of course the whole town has been rebuilt. When you came back to Kljuc in 1996, I think it was, what did the town look like?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was in very bad state of repair. Most of the houses had been torched. They didn't have roofs. It -- it looked destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I wanted to show you, then, two photographs that were at least taken nearer to the time. Could you first of all look at divider 65. Oh, sorry. I should have said it's 10265.7. Now, that was taken in 2001. Are you able to identify the building at all?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is the building in the local commune of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you say the name again, please, Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is the building in the local commune of Pec on the road from Kljuc to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the nationality of the -- the people who lived in that commune?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The population was of mixed ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say -- do you know exactly what that building was before it was destroyed like that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This used to be a shop or a store, and the building also housed the premises of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was the owner of the store?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P944, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you came back to Kljuc in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if you're going on to something else, this is the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just going to finish this. And then I'm going to finish this topic because that's the end of the photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you came back to Kljuc in 1996, were any of the mosques still standing?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: All of them had been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Egrlic. I think there's going to be a break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I thought we'd done with maps and photographs, but I just realised that I think we need to have one more map. Could we have the one that's behind divider 26, please. 3113. Just so we can ... Yes. That -- is that right? It just -- that shows the -- Kljuc again, but this time we can see the municipalities that bordered with it, namely Bosanski Petrovac, Sanski Most, Banja Luka, and then we needn't bother about Drvar and Mrkonjic Grad. Yes. And that's just actually one further thing that I ought perhaps to ask you -- actually, no, I won't. It's on another map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that simply be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P945, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Egrlic, I'm just going to ask you some questions now for the remainder of the time about some documents that relate to matters and events that you described when you gave evidence last time. First of all, you told us about some of the leaders of the political parties and about Vinko Kondic as chief of the SJB. Are you aware that Vinko Kondic is presently standing trial in the state court of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. There's a man called Jovo Banjac who figures in some of these documents. What was his position in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And of what nationality was he?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you talked in your testimony in the Brdjanin case --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this is page -- at page 10527 and the following pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- about the attempts to join the Autonomous Region of Krajina and its predecessor, the community of municipalities. I want you to have a look, please, first of all at a document which is 65 ter 778, and it's divider 27 for Mr. Egrlic. Now, this is a document which doesn't have a date, but it refers to the founding of the -- or the meeting held on the 10th of April, 1991, by the Municipal Assembly, that it would remain in the Banja Luka community of municipalities, and then it talks about the earlier decision regarding "The Kljuc municipality is hereby confirmed." Are you able to recognise the stamp and the signature?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it says -- it's typed "Jovo Banjac." So you recognise his signature, do you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I don't want to go into this because you dealt with this extensively in your testimony, but effectively I think you, the SDA, and the MBO, objected to -- to the joining of this -- of Kljuc to this particular Banja Luka community of municipalities and then the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Can you just very briefly tell the Court what the objection was.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We understood that this was a para-state creation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not understand the rest of the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And then we believed that this would not lead to equal rights of all the nations living in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Mr. Egrlic. Again it was the problem they didn't hear you. Could you repeat the full answer. You said you believed this was a para-state creation.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was an anti-constitutional creation. It was a para-state creation in the territory of an internationally recognised country, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And by "para-state," can you just explain what you mean again briefly.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: What I mean is that given all the elements, that part of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina appeared to be a state, was a state-like creation with all its organs and that it was contrary to the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that it could not be accepted for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you also said it -- you also believed it wouldn't lead to the equal rights of all nations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, may that be marked -- admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P946, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then can you have a quick look, please, at 65 ter 785. Divider 31 for you. And again, can you identify the signature of Jovo Banjac? It seems to be the formal commitment of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P947, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next I want to move to the events of May the 7th and those that preceded it. You told the Court when you testified before about the changes in the insignia of the police, the fact that Serbian flags flew over the Municipal Assembly on May the 7th, and you also told the Court that before that you and others had had a meeting in Banja Luka with Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll just turn up the page of the transcript for the note. Yes. It's page -- in the Brdjanin transcript, page 10549 and following.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you described to the Court in the Brdjanin case that you; Mr. Omer Filipovic; Mr. Banjac; and the two Kondics, Vinko and Veljko, went to Banja Luka to see Zupljanin about the changes in the insignia of the police. Can you just give us, please, a little bit more detail of that meeting. First of all, in order to go to Banja Luka, did you have to pass the Manjaca training grounds?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you passed them, what was happening that you could see?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were check-points and one couldn't pass through without an ID or without being escorted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was manning the check-points?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, whether it was the police or the army, they wore multi-colour camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you passed Manjaca itself, was anything actually happening on those training grounds that you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Egrlic, you're being asked to repeat the answer. They didn't catch it again.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I wasn't paying attention to what was going on the training grounds, so I couldn't see anything really.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, during the course of your discussions with Mr. Zupljanin, did he say anything to you and the others about his opinion of Bosniaks or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, when it came to the change of insignia, that it was a fait accompli, that it was a concluded matter and not to be discussed any more. And that those changes would take place, and that police members would start wearing new insignia instead of the old insignia and that the new insignia would have the Serbian tricolour flag. He even gave us three berets for us to see what they looked like. And the policemen who were Bosniaks refused to accept such uniforms, and he said that it wasn't really polite of them to do that, and the meeting concluded. It wasn't a successful meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Other than about what was going to happen with uniforms, did he say anything about the relationship between Bosniaks and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was really a jocular conversation between him and Omer Filipovic. He claimed that Filipovic was really a descendant of some Filip, and this is how they ended up with that last name. There was also discussion of how Bosniaks were really part of a Serbian nation, how they were really originally Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That's all I want to ask you about that meeting additional to what you've already said about it. Did you come to hear about a Crisis Staff being set up in Kljuc? And I'm talking now about before May the 7th.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I'm talking about now a Crisis Staff from the SDS.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want you to have a look for a moment, please, then at one of the documents that I think was admitted as part of your package.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I should have marked this, and I've just not done that. No. Wait a minute. Sorry. It's not part of the package. It's -- would Your Honour give me one moment while I just check it before I waste time on the booklet. No. Forget that. I'm sorry, Your Honour, because it -- to find the document which was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can I now move, please, to the -- what happened on the 7th of May and after the 7th of May. And you dealt with that in your testimony in Brdjanin at pages 10559, following. Now, was there -- after the insignia had changed and the Serbs took over, was there a call that weapons should be surrendered?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how was that announcement made?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was announced on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that immediately after May the 7th or later?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Somewhat later, some 10 to 15 days later or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look then, please, at a series of documents that relate to what happened on or around the 27th of May. By the 27th of May, where were you? Were you still in the town, or had you, by that stage, left?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was in the town until the 7th of May. But after the 7th of May I was no longer there because the army had entered the town, the 6th Krajina Brigade. They took up all important locations, intersections. They introduced a curfew. One couldn't move about. So I stopped going into town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to ask you, then, in relation to the curfew and the rest, and you couldn't move around, could you look please at the document behind divider 34, and it's 65 ter 800. This is an order issued on the 27th of May by the Crisis Staff, signed by Mr. Banjac. Again, can you identify his signature?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it says: "Citizens are prohibited from moving ... without special permission from the Kljuc Public Security Station." Were you aware of that order?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I knew of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P948, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could we have 65 ter 801, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it's divider 35 for you. This is obviously the minutes, we can see, handwritten of the Crisis Staff meeting of the 27th of May, which talks about the -- first that "the legitimacy of the decisions of the autonomous region Crisis Staff are affirmed." And then number 3: "By June the 1st, 1992, remove all non-Serbian personnel from positions which allow independent decision-making and securing property." Item 10: "The relationship of the military ... to the civilian ... that the military will execute the orders of the civilian ... while the civilian authorities will not interfere with the way these orders are carried out." And then finally on this that I want to ask you about. Item 15: "Suspend --" oh, yes, sorry. For the screen, if that's what the accused are looking at, that's on the third page. Yes. "Suspend Osman Avdic, Zeljko Bakovic, Kapetanovic, employees of the Municipal Council for national defence immediately, and then authorise Tihomir Dakic and others to find a solutions to fill the vacancies." First, did you know the first three people who were named there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did. Avdic, Osman used to work at the Secretariat for National Defence. Later on he was found shot dead together with other citizens in the Biljani local commune. Zeljko, an ethnic Croat, I used to know him too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And who was Tihomir Dakic? Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was vice-president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And -- and what nationality was he?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: A Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So he was your vice-president, was he, when you were president of the Executive Board?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P949, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you, sir, go back in the binder, for you, to number 32, I think it is. Yes. And it's -- sorry. It's 65 ter 1106. Now, the date on this appears to be the 3rd of February, 1992, but from the context I'm not sure that can be right, but it reads that: "From the beginning of the war to today, the Serbian armed forces, conducting fast and energetic operations, have completely broken up the Muslim combat formations ..." It then goes on to say after a bit of "hardened extremists" verbiage: "... we again call on the Muslim people to hand over their remaining weapons and to help capture and happened hand over these lunatics," and so on and so forth. Did you hear a radio announcement around this time along those lines? And when I say "this time," I don't mean February 1992, I mean around May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This reflects or corresponds to the period of June more than anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what I thought about the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P950, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then finally on this topic could you have a look, please, at the document behind divider 36 for you, and it's 803, 65 ter 803. This again is the Crisis Staff issuing an order this time the following day, 28th of May, calling on all citizens who own illegally acquired weapons to hand them over. And then in item 2: "The Kljuc municipality Crisis Staff orders members of Muslim nationality from the Ramici and Krasulje areas to hand over those responsible for yesterday's crime against the deputy commander of the police station." Do you know what that refers to in paragraph 2?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In the local commune of Krasulje, the local police commander from Kljuc was killed, and I suppose that the reference is to that event.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know the -- do you know personally the circumstances in which he came to be killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know from what I heard. I heard that the manoeuvre police -- platoon of the police started seizing weapons in the village of Krasulje and that they opened fire on the village guards. The fire was returned, and that's -- the commander of the police station got killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Item 4: "We ... order citizens of Muslim nationality from the Egrlic and Pudin Han areas to hand over those responsible for the attack on unarmed soldiers who were in an organised transport from Knin to Banja Luka." Do you know to what that refers?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I also know that in the territory of Pudin Han an incident took place. The troops that were transported by lorries opened fire on the settlement and the mosque in Pudin Han, and then in the Busija sector fire was returned, and that resulted in an armed incident, or that was the armed incident in question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Then they call upon Omer Filipovic to surrender. Then the White Eagles and the armed forces who have returned from the battle-field are ordered to put themselves under the command of the 30th division. And then finally 7: "All citizens of Muslim nationality from the Velagici local commune and part of the Kljuc local commune ... who are currently in the combat action zone and who want peace are hereby ordered to gather at the SIP, the timber processing company, by 1.00." Do you know what happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I am not receiving any interpretation. I can't hear a thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Item -- I won't read the paragraph again, Mr. Egrlic. In paragraph 7 the Muslim nationality -- persons of Muslim nationality are ordered to gather at the timber processing company. Did you understand what --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. I see the witness is shaking his head.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He still can't hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I guess he's not receiving any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- can you hear? No. Can you hear me saying, "Paragraph 7 of the document"? No. We appear to have a technical hitch at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm advised that instead of rising we should just hang on for a few minutes and see what happens. Can you hear me? This is a test. Am I coming through?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're going to have to take a break. --- Break taken at 4.39 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As we resume, for those of you who might be curious, notwithstanding these unintended breaks caused by technical problems, it would be simpler, nevertheless, to take the usual breaks at the expected times. So at 5.20, we will take the break. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you now hear me?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just was asking you about paragraph 7 of this document that we were looking at ordering Muslim citizens to go to the timber processing company. Do you know if people went there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to those people who went there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were several places where people were collected. One was a warehouse in SIP. Another one was the school Nikola Mackic in Kljuc, and the football stadium. That's where they perform some checks, interrogations, and then they were transported --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear where.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And some were returned home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch where you said they were transported to.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: From the places that were designated as collection points and where they interrogated people, and from there people were sent to Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Yes. That's all I want to ask you about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As exhibit P951.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm little bit confused. Because the question was, Did the witness know? How the witness can know, if he wasn't there? What is the source of his information about these documents? That's --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You, yourself, were taken to Manjaca. Were there other inmates of Manjaca there? Sorry, that's a bad question. Forget that. Did you talk to other people who had been brought to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was it those people who told you from where they had come when they were sent to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Can I then move fairly swiftly - because I'm afraid we're running out of time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, you have 20 minutes left, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've just been reminded of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- to the question of dismissals. I want you to look at a couple of other documents, please. First of all, could we have a look at divider 30. Oh, sorry. 65 ter number 3053. This is a document being submitted to the Municipal Assembly in response to a request for managerial staff of Muslim and Croat ethnicity. The people who are named here, did you know some of them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were these people all dismissed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P952, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Exhibit behind divider 39, which is -- no, I don't -- don't worry, because it's already part of the package. That's part of the 92 ter package. Could we have a look, though, please, at the document behind divider 41, please, which is 2635. Judge Kapetanovic is ordered to be removed. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was he dismissed as a result of this order?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could that be, please, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P953, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next document is at 42 and is 2636. I'm pointing Mr. Dimitrijevic -- we're still on the last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Actually, Your Honours, these are all on the same -- if that's all right, could I ask they all be admitted. They're all relating to dismissals and appointments of Judges rather than taking him through each one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: How many comprise the package?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They are documents -- I think they're all 65 ters one after the other. Yes, they are. It's 236, 237, 238, and 239. Oh, 26, sorry. it's 2636, 2637, 2638, 2639, all of which were on our 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours -- 65 ter number 2636 will be Exhibit P954. 65 ter 2637 will be Exhibit P955. 65 ter number 2638 will be P957 -- 956, Your Honours. And 65 ter number 2639 will be P957.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then finally, or finally -- in your evidence on the Brdjanin case you gave evidence about how your wife was forced to sign a document relinquishing her property to the Kljuc municipality, and you dealt with that. I'd like you to have a look at one document on those lines as well, please. Could you look, please, at the document behind divider 47 and 65 ter number 3013. Mr. Egrlic, this document dated the 10th of August, 1992, is signed by Mr. Sistek, I think, although it's been mistyped. Did you know -- any way, did you know that -- the person who was signing over their property here? Or persons? There are a number of them, a lot of them, including Omer Filipovic, apparently. Did you know them all?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P958, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, very brief -- briefly, sir. Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'm wrong. Where do you see their property? Were do you see that in this text?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is what he said about those -- he was asked about this, and he said this in his testimony. I can give you the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Because I don't find in this document the term property. That's my --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I understand that. But this is what he said it actually meant when he testified. And I agree the document doesn't say, "I leave my property to the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just deal, please, briefly with what happened to you and then take you immediately to Manjaca. You were, I think, arrested at a check-point, and as you've explained, you were beaten when you were taken to the SUP, and that's at page 10562 of the transcript. You were then taken to hospital and beaten again outside the hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think it's right that all you can say about the people who beat you is that they were in uniform, but you're unable to say whether they were army or police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter didn't hear your answer again.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were reserve policemen and troops as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you're able to say that they were reserve policemen how? Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I knew those who had beaten me by names because we went to the same grammar school. They were only a year older than me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. From Kljuc were you taken to Stari Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
